baseline.title: Writing audit based on Dan Lovejoy's no-slop rules

rules.title: Not only, but also

check.instructions: Does this sentence use 'not only ... but also' to make a point sound bigger, rather than to join two separate facts the reader needs?
check.criteria_true: The construction adds emphasis.
check.criteria_false: The sentence does not use it, or uses it to join two needed facts.

rules.falsifier: The construction adds emphasis.

rules.title: Not only, but also

check.coverage: Every sentence of this complete article is checked; the article contains the pattern if any sentence contains it.

rules.falsifier: The construction adds emphasis.

rules.title: Not just

check.instructions: Does this sentence use 'not just' to make something sound grander than the facts it states?
check.criteria_true: 'Not just' inflates the description.
check.criteria_false: The sentence does not use 'not just', or uses it to add a stated fact.

rules.falsifier: 'Not just' inflates the description.

rules.title: Not just

check.coverage: Every sentence of this complete article is checked; the article contains the pattern if any sentence contains it.

rules.falsifier: 'Not just' inflates the description.

rules.title: Sentence-opening range

check.instructions: Does this sentence start with a 'from ... to ...' range?
check.criteria_true: The sentence starts with a range introduced by 'from' and 'to'.
check.criteria_false: The sentence does not start with that range construction.

rules.falsifier: The sentence starts with a range introduced by 'from' and 'to'.

rules.title: Sentence-opening range

check.coverage: Every sentence of this complete article is checked; the article contains the pattern if any sentence contains it.

rules.falsifier: The sentence starts with a range introduced by 'from' and 'to'.

rules.title: Whether you are

check.instructions: Does this sentence address the reader with 'whether you are X or Y' or a similar pair of reader types?
check.criteria_true: The sentence addresses the reader with such a pair.
check.criteria_false: The sentence does not address the reader that way.

rules.falsifier: The sentence addresses the reader with such a pair.

rules.title: Whether you are

check.coverage: Every sentence of this complete article is checked; the article contains the pattern if any sentence contains it.

rules.falsifier: The sentence addresses the reader with such a pair.

rules.title: Today's landscape

check.instructions: The passage is the text of the subject part; the reader's brief is in the policy part. Does the article introduce its topic with a vague claim about today's world?
check.criteria_true: It uses a vague claim about today's world as an introduction.
check.criteria_false: It does not use that introduction.

rules.falsifier: It uses a vague claim about today's world as an introduction.

rules.title: Trailing -ing clause

check.instructions: Does the sentence end with a comma followed by a present-participle clause?
check.criteria_true: A complete main clause is followed by a comma and a trailing clause whose verb is a present participle.
check.criteria_false: No such trailing clause appears.

rules.falsifier: A complete main clause is followed by a comma and a trailing clause whose verb is a present participle.

rules.title: Trailing -ing clause

check.coverage: Every sentence of this complete article is checked; the article contains the pattern if any sentence contains it.

rules.falsifier: A complete main clause is followed by a comma and a trailing clause whose verb is a present participle.

rules.title: Opening rhetorical question

check.instructions: The passage is the text of the subject part; the reader's brief is in the policy part. Does the opening ask a rhetorical question?
check.criteria_true: The opening asks a question for effect.
check.criteria_false: The opening does not ask a question for effect.

rules.falsifier: The opening asks a question for effect.

rules.title: Recap ending

check.instructions: Does the article end with a paragraph that summarizes earlier points?
check.criteria_true: The closing paragraph recaps points already made in the article, even if it also adds a next step.
check.criteria_false: The closing paragraph gives new information or actions without recapping earlier points.

rules.falsifier: The closing paragraph recaps points already made in the article, even if it also adds a next step.

rules.title: Preview promises

check.instructions: Does the article tell the reader what it will explain or cover later?
check.criteria_true: The writer announces the article's later content or promises what it will teach.
check.criteria_false: The article gives information directly, describes future events or actions, or quotes someone else's promise without making its own preview.

rules.falsifier: The writer announces the article's later content or promises what it will teach.

rules.title: Repeating the request

check.instructions: Does the article restate the reader's request before answering it?
check.criteria_true: The opening repeats or paraphrases the reader's request before giving the answer.
check.criteria_false: The opening gives an answer or relevant facts directly, without restating the request.

rules.falsifier: The opening repeats or paraphrases the reader's request before giving the answer.

rules.title: Vague hands-on claim

check.instructions: Does this sentence say 'hands-on' without saying what the reader will do?
check.criteria_true: It says 'hands-on' without naming an activity.
check.criteria_false: The phrase is absent, or the sentence names a specific activity.

rules.falsifier: It says 'hands-on' without naming an activity.

rules.title: Vague hands-on claim

check.coverage: Every sentence of this complete article is checked; the article contains the pattern if any sentence contains it.

rules.falsifier: It says 'hands-on' without naming an activity.

check.instructions: Does this sentence say 'real-world' without naming a specific situation?
check.criteria_true: It says 'real-world' without naming a situation.
check.criteria_false: The phrase is absent, or the sentence names a specific situation.

rules.falsifier: It says 'real-world' without naming a situation.

check.coverage: Every sentence of this complete article is checked; the article contains the pattern if any sentence contains it.

check.criteria_true: The contrast works as a slogan.
check.criteria_false: There is no such contrast, or it corrects a stated misunderstanding.

check.criteria_false: The paragraph uses complete sentences, or a fragment only once for a stated purpose.

rules.title: Adjective triplet

check.instructions: Does this sentence describe one thing with three praising adjectives in a row?
check.criteria_true: Three praising adjectives describe the same thing.
check.criteria_false: The sentence has no such run of three praising adjectives.

rules.falsifier: Three praising adjectives describe the same thing.

check.coverage: Every sentence of this complete article is checked; the article contains the pattern if any sentence contains it.

rules.title: Listed stock vocabulary
rules.falsifier: A listed term occurs in visible Markdown prose, including headings, lists and quoted prose.

rules.title: Buffer phrases
rules.falsifier: A listed buffer occurs in visible Markdown prose.

rules.title: Filler transitions

check.instructions: Does this sentence use one of these filler phrases: at the end of the day, when it comes to, at its core, let's break it down, or this is where X comes in, where X is any subject?
check.criteria_true: A listed filler phrase appears.
check.criteria_false: None of those phrases appears.

rules.falsifier: A listed filler phrase appears.

rules.title: Filler transitions

check.coverage: Every sentence of this complete article is checked; the article contains the pattern if any sentence contains it.

rules.falsifier: A listed filler phrase appears.

rules.title: Software and mathematics personification

check.instructions: Does the article say that software or mathematics thinks, intends, wants, believes, decides, understands or prefers?
check.criteria_true: It assigns a model, algorithm, program or mathematical object a thought, intention, desire, opinion, understanding or preference.
check.criteria_false: It describes only computation or human mental abilities, or explicitly denies those abilities to software or mathematics.

rules.falsifier: It assigns a model, algorithm, program or mathematical object a thought, intention, desire, opinion, understanding or preference.

rules.title: Inflated substitutes for is

check.instructions: Does this sentence use 'serves as', 'featuring', 'boasting' or 'presenting' to say what something is?
check.criteria_true: A listed phrase says what something is.
check.criteria_false: Those phrases are absent, or describe an action rather than what something is.

rules.falsifier: A listed phrase says what something is.

rules.title: Inflated substitutes for is

check.coverage: Every sentence of this complete article is checked; the article contains the pattern if any sentence contains it.

rules.falsifier: A listed phrase says what something is.

rules.title: Synonym cycling

check.instructions: Does this paragraph use different words to name the same person, group, or thing?
check.criteria_true: Different synonymous nouns name the same person, group, or thing.
check.criteria_false: There are no interchangeable names for the same subject. Pronouns and nouns for different subjects do not count.

rules.falsifier: Different synonymous nouns name the same person, group, or thing.

rules.title: Synonym cycling

check.coverage: Every paragraph of this complete article is checked; the article contains the pattern if any paragraph contains it.

rules.falsifier: Different synonymous nouns name the same person, group, or thing.

check.criteria_true: It relies on unnamed experts, studies or research.
check.criteria_false: It names its source, or makes no such appeal.

rules.title: Announcing a topic

check.criteria_false: The paragraph gives facts or instructions directly.

rules.falsifier: The paragraph announces a topic without giving its information.

rules.title: Here is preamble

check.instructions: The passage is the text of the subject part; the reader's brief is in the policy part. Does the opening announce the answer with wording such as 'here is' or 'below you will find'?
check.criteria_true: The opening announces the answer before giving it.
check.criteria_false: The opening gives information directly.

rules.falsifier: The opening announces the answer before giving it.

rules.title: First requested instruction

check.instructions: The article field holds an article and the brief field holds the reader's brief. Copy the first sentence of the article that gives the reader an instruction the brief asks for.

first_instruction.description: That sentence, copied exactly from the article, as a list of one item. Empty when the article gives no such instruction.

rules.falsifier: A later sentence, an invented sentence or one that is not a requested instruction is copied, or the first one is missed.

rules.title: Delayed answer

check.instructions: The article field holds an article and the brief field holds the reader's brief. Does background the brief did not ask for come before the article's first requested instruction? When first_instruction is present, a helper copied that instruction from the article; rely on it only where the article confirms it.
check.criteria_true: Background the reader did not ask for delays the first requested instruction.
check.criteria_false: The first requested instruction comes first, or only requested context precedes it.

rules.falsifier: Background the reader did not ask for delays the first requested instruction.

rules.title: Three-item list
rules.falsifier: A CommonMark list contains exactly three direct items, with nested lists counted separately.

rules.title: Narrative broken into bullets

check.instructions: The passage is the text of the subject part; the reader's brief is in the policy part. Does a bullet list tell a continuous story instead of listing separate points?
check.criteria_true: Bullets split a continuous story into pieces.
check.criteria_false: Bullets are absent or list separate points.

rules.falsifier: Bullets split a continuous story into pieces.

rules.title: Bold label and colon bullets

check.instructions: The passage is the text of the subject part; the reader's brief is in the policy part. Does a bullet begin with a bold label followed by a colon and an explanatory sentence?
check.criteria_true: That bold-label bullet pattern appears.
check.criteria_false: That pattern is absent.

rules.falsifier: That bold-label bullet pattern appears.

rules.title: Bold emphasis in prose
rules.falsifier: A prose phrase uses bold for emphasis.

rules.title: More than one em dash
rules.falsifier: There are at least two em dashes.

rules.title: Paragraph sentence-length rule
rules.falsifier: A CommonMark prose paragraph outside lists lacks either required sentence length under the documented Unicode counting convention.

rules.title: Generic sympathy and reassurance

check.instructions: Does the article offer generic sympathy or reassurance about the reader's difficulties?
check.criteria_true: It uses a stock expression of understanding, sympathy or reassurance about the reader's difficulties. Giving practical advice does not cancel that expression.
check.criteria_false: It contains no such generic expression. A specific factual account of someone's experience is not generic sympathy.

rules.falsifier: It uses a stock expression of understanding, sympathy or reassurance about the reader's difficulties. Giving practical advice does not cancel that expression.

rules.falsifier: It starts with a stock assistant greeting.

rules.title: Repeated paragraph shape

check.criteria_true: Several paragraphs repeat the same sentence pattern without a reason.
